column2: # Drop the channel-name header if present. Detect it by row count, not by content:
# as.numeric("NaN") is a valid number, so a content test would misfire on the leading NaN.
stop(basename(path), ": expected 3 channel rows (optionally after a header), found ",
length(lines), ". This file is not in the instrument's wide format.")
time <- to_num(lines[1]); disp <- to_num(lines[2]); force <- to_num(lines[3])
stop(basename(path), ": channel rows have unequal lengths (",
stop(basename(path), ": only ", n, " sample(s); too short to integrate.")
# Count missing values before filling, so the QC record survives into the output.
n_na <- c(time = sum(is.na(time)), disp = sum(is.na(disp)), force = sum(is.na(force)))
" missing sample(s) away from the start (index ",
"); zero-filled - check the QC plot.", call. = FALSE)
# Integration assumes increasing time. Sort rather than trust, and say so if it was not.
warning(basename(path), ": time was not monotonic; samples reordered before integration.",
o <- order(time); time <- time[o]; disp <- disp[o]; force <- force[o]
list(time = time, displacement = disp, force = force, n_na = n_na)
# Area under the force/time curve, by trapezoid, on the raw trace.
# The previous version called loess() then integrated `loess()$y`, which is the response, not
# `$fitted` - so it was already integrating the raw trace, but on a grid from
# approx(n = length(x)) that did not line up with the diff(x) it was multiplied by. This is the
# same quantity, computed correctly. Across the current 375 traces the two agree to a median of
# 0.006% and a maximum of 2.1%. loess() is still fitted below, for the QC plot only.
